nfl.oneThing: Puka Nacua is expected to miss about two months, which the report says effectively ends the Rams receiver's 2026 season. The Colts also released Daniel Jones, leaving Indy at 3–8.

headlines.title: Puka Nacua out for about two months
headlines.summary: Puka Nacua is expected to be out for the next two months, which the report says essentially ends his 2026 season. Rams fans had been feeling better about the team, with a survey finding over 60% believed the club was headed in the right direction. The Rams are 6–4 and currently outside the NFC's seven seeds. Davante Adams is still on injured reserve and McVay says he isn't ready yet.
headlines.whyItMatters: Losing the team's best offensive player for the rest of the year makes the Rams' push for a playoff spot much harder, especially with the NFC wild-card race this tight.

headlines.title: Colts release Daniel Jones
headlines.summary: The Colts have released quarterback Daniel Jones, who was in the Colts' 26–3 loss to the Texans. Jones went 12 of 27 for 144 yards with no touchdowns and one interception. Indy also didn't trade its quarterback or Jonathan Taylor at the deadline. Giants head coach John Harbaugh was reportedly shocked by the move, since Jones is a former Giants teammate. The Colts are 3–8 and 12th in the AFC.
headlines.whyItMatters: The release leaves the Colts' direction in doubt after they stood pat at the deadline, and it puts Jones on the market for teams such as the Cardinals and Patriots, both linked to him in coverage.

headlines.title: Carson Beck's back flares up, Josh Johnson set to start
headlines.summary: Cardinals rookie Carson Beck is dealing with back spasms that flared up on a problem that has lingered all season, and he missed practice for a second straight day. Coach Mike LaFleur says veteran Josh Johnson is being prepared to start Sunday in Kansas City. LaFleur doesn't think the injury will keep Beck out for multiple weeks, but he's not ruling him out for Sunday either. ProFootballTalk lists Beck as questionable. Arizona is 3–7, while the Chiefs are 7–2.
headlines.whyItMatters: Arizona is already well out of the playoff picture, so the focus is on the quarterback's health and what the Cardinals can learn from Johnson's start.

headlines.title: 49ers and Vikings meet in Mexico City
headlines.summary: The 8–1 49ers play the 7–2 Vikings on Sunday in Mexico City. San Francisco's offence averages a league-leading 399.8 yards per game and 31.2 points, second in the NFL. Minnesota allows a league-low 14 points a game and 273.3 yards, second fewest. The 49ers also lead the league in offensive points per possession at three.
headlines.whyItMatters: A win would strengthen San Francisco's grip on the NFC's top seed, while Minnesota would be proving it can beat the NFC's best.

teamNews.title: Brock Bowers questionable with ankle and quad
teamNews.text: Bowers is listed as questionable for Sunday at Denver. Coach Klint Kubiak said Friday that the tight end's ankle and quad issues are being monitored, and Bowers said his availability remains up in the air. Bowers' recent production is down on his season average, with 5.2 receptions over the last five games against 6.3 for the year.

The Broncos are 7–2 and ninth in points allowed, and they are vulnerable to both the air and ground game. After Denver, the Raiders face the Browns in Cleveland.

contextCard.title: How the NFL waiver wire works
contextCard.body: When a team releases a player, he goes onto the waiver wire, where other teams can claim him. Claims are awarded in order of priority, with teams that finished with worse records first in line. If no team claims him, the player becomes a free agent and can sign anywhere. This is why a released quarterback like Daniel Jones can draw interest from several teams at once.

nba.oneThing: The Warriors have lost five straight, including four by 20 or more points, and Stephen Curry is out with an abdominal injury.

headlines.title: Warriors in free fall without Curry
headlines.summary: The Warriors lost 126–98 at Memphis, their fifth straight loss. They have lost four straight games by 20 or more points, tying the longest such streak in franchise history, set in 1997–98. Stephen Curry is out with a right abdominal injury. Jaylen Wells led Memphis with 22 points, and Cedric Coward added 19 points and five threes. Charles Bassey had 16 points and 13 rebounds for Golden State. The Grizzlies are 12–4 and fourth in the West.
headlines.whyItMatters: Golden State is 8–8 and 10th in the West, and the losing streak is pulling it further from the top of the conference while Curry is sidelined.

headlines.title: Brandon Ingram set for Clippers debut
headlines.summary: Brandon Ingram is expected to make his season debut for the Clippers on Monday against the Rockets, according to reports. He has been out since May, when surgery to remove a heel bone spur revealed a partially torn Achilles tendon. The Clippers are 4–10 and 13th in the West after losing 124–112 to the Spurs.
headlines.whyItMatters: Ingram's return gives Los Angeles a major piece back after a poor start, and it will show how much the Clippers can rebuild around him.

headlines.title: Caleb Wilson's injuries are 'bad luck', doctors say
headlines.summary: Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson has had three hand-related injuries in the past year. He fractured his right hand on November 12 while trying to knock the ball away from Victor Wembanyama. Wilson says doctors told him the injuries aren't connected. He missed the NCAA tournament last season after surgery on a broken right thumb, and he missed six games with a broken left hand. He has been in a sling and may not travel with the team while the Bulls play nine of their next 10 games at home.
headlines.whyItMatters: Chicago is 4–10 and 13th in the East, and Wilson's availability will shape how the rookie develops in his first season.

teamNews.title: Dylan Harper out with hip soreness
teamNews.text: Dylan Harper is out after slipping on the court, with hip soreness. Sources say he will be out one to three weeks with a hip strain, while ClutchPoints reports two to three weeks. The reports leave the exact return date open.

teamNews.title: Tobias Harris out with calf strain
teamNews.text: Tobias Harris is likely to miss time with a left calf strain and is not expected back until early December, according to reports. The absence gives the Spurs a chance to rethink their rotation.

teamNews.title: Wembanyama's new shot came from a blister
teamNews.text: Victor Wembanyama says his new 'shunk' shot was done because of a blister on his hand. He avoided a dunk in a viral clip from the Clippers win.

teamNews.title: Spurs bounce back from the Pistons loss
teamNews.text: San Antonio beat the Clippers 124–112 at home after a loss to Detroit. Stephon Castle had 12 assists and Julian Champagnie scored 20 points, while Harrison Barnes and Jordan McLaughlin added veteran depth.

Tyler Herro had 19 points for the Bucks, who fell to 1–15 despite a solid effort from Nate Ament, with 18 points and nine rebounds.

recaps.text: New York edged Minnesota 102–99 in a tight finish. Karl-Anthony Towns had 22 points, 12 rebounds, four assists and three blocks, and Jalen Brunson added 21 points and seven assists. Jonathan Kuminga scored 23 for the Timberwolves and LaMelo Ball had 15 points, eight rebounds and eight assists, but Minnesota couldn't hold the lead. The Knicks are 9–6 and sixth in the East.
